summary: Four JSON-store services (CommandPresetService, WorkspaceService, TerminalShortcutService, RecoveryOptionService) use a fixed .tmp path for write-then-rename, so concurrent dev instances sharing a worktree collide (EPERM/ENOENT/torn writes) and can crash the process on boot; fix with a shared atomic-write helper (unique tmp name, atomically-published .bak, bounded rename retry, own-tmp-only cleanup).
key_entities: REL-BGSTAB-020 (prior in-process serialization fix, scoped to a single process's promise chain)
ambiguities: Whether this should land as a new BGSTAB requirement or as an amendment/extension to REL-BGSTAB-020's existing text (brief only says the in-process fix left the cross-process case untouched, not how the requirement graph should represent that).
Concrete bounded-retry parameters (max attempt count, backoff delay/curve) for the rename-on-EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY path are unspecified.

Whether the four services must call one single shared helper module/function, or four independent implementations that merely follow the same pattern (brief says 'shared atomic-write helper' but does not name/locate it or specify its signature).

Final behavior when bounded retries are exhausted is unspecified: brief says the current unguarded crash-on-init behavior is the problem, but does not state whether after retries fail the service should throw (and if so, whether index.ts's uncaught-exception-crash path is intended to remain) or degrade gracefully.
Whether the same unique-tmp + atomic-publish treatment for the .bak copy must also get its own bounded retry on rename failure, or only the primary destination rename does.
implied_requirements: A failed write must never delete or otherwise disturb a peer process's own in-flight tmp file (cleanup must be scoped strictly to the tmp path this write created).
Under concurrent cross-process writes, the destination file must never observably contain partially-written (torn) JSON at any point another process could read it.
If all retries are exhausted, the pre-existing last-known-good destination file must be left intact rather than being replaced by corrupt or partial content.
The fix must not regress or duplicate the already-serialized in-process concurrency behavior established by REL-BGSTAB-020 for WorkspaceService.
The four target services must end up behaving consistently (same collision-avoidance semantics), implying some form of shared/reusable implementation rather than four divergent bespoke fixes.
Test evidence and requirement text must record the Linux/WSL2 manifestation (ENOENT / torn tmp) actually observed, and must not claim to reproduce or verify the Windows EPERM case natively.

The RED test must exercise two independent service instances against one shared data file with a payload large enough to span multiple event-loop ticks, per the WorkspaceServiceFlushConcurrency.test.ts technique — an empty/small fixture is explicitly called out as insufficient to expose the defect.
semantic_equivalences: 'atomic write' == the existing writeFile(dest+'.tmp') -> copyFile(dest, dest+'.bak') -> rename(dest+'.tmp', dest) pattern, made collision-safe.

'cross-process write race' (this issue) != the 'in-process concurrent flush' race already fixed by REL-BGSTAB-020's promise-chain serialization — same symptom family (rename failure / corruption), different root cause and different process boundary.
Windows 'EPERM on rename' and Linux/WSL2 'ENOENT / torn tmp content' are treated as the same underlying shared-tmp-path collision surfacing differently per OS, not two separate bugs.

'unique tmp name per write' (pid+random) removes the shared-tmp collision and the torn-tmp hazard, but is explicitly NOT a substitute for bounded rename retry, which addresses a separate residual hazard (two instances still rename onto the same destination).
